reason: Structural CD19 location: defaultPathOperations/pathOperationsFor confines Node path and file-URL conversion behind named string-only PathOperations. Reviewer consumers use this existing adapter; no platform types are exported. The additional module-location capability is a deliberate reviewer-port paydown boundary decision.

Structural CD19 location: defaultSidecarFileReader/defaultFileKindPort/defaultFileTextPort confines filesystem and temporary-directory runtime access. Review scripts and hermetic fixtures consume named text/file capabilities with production factories; no Node file/stat types are exported. Adding writes and temporary scratch lifecycle here reuses the existing filesystem boundary instead of opening a second Node fs wrapping site.

Structural CD19 location: defaultReviewProcessPort is the deliberate process boundary for reviewer entrypoints and hermetic subprocess fixtures. It confines Node child execution, environment, standard streams and termination; consumers receive string/status data and named capabilities, never ChildProcess or stream types.

Structural CD19 location: defaultContentDigestPort confines node:crypto sha256 hashing behind a ContentDigestPort whose single capability takes text or bytes and returns a hex string. Consumers receive the digest string, never a Hash object. This is the single wrapping site for content hashing in the rin plugin's tools.

whys.why: Why does plugins/rin/tools/rin-harness-content-digest.ts import a platform runtime surface at all?
whys.because: The rin-gates derivation selftest's landed-binding cases compute an independent sha256 of a merge patch to check the verdict emitter's digest, and sha256 hashing is provided only by the runtime's node:crypto.
whys.evidence: plugins/rin/tools/rin-gates/rin-gates-derivation-selftest.spec.ts mergePatchDigestIn, used by case E1 (emitter digest equals an independently computed sha256 of the merge patch).

whys.why: Why is that hashing not left as a direct import in the selftest?
whys.because: The selftest is a carved file that fork PR #4 touches, so CD-46 revokes its carve-out, and CD-19 then requires its stdlib dependencies to arrive through ports; no hashing port existed in the plugin to route through.
whys.evidence: HailsTails/aidlc-workflows PR #4 Source checks: rin-harness-carve-out-decay.ts reported [CD-19] plugins/rin/tools/rin-gates/rin-gates-derivation-selftest.spec.ts; .constitution-carve-outs/cd-19.json entry for that file listed node:crypto among its inherited imports.

whys.why: Why does the default binding live in this file?
whys.because: CD-21 requires each port to ship its default production factory co-located in its own module, so the port type and its node:crypto binding form one canonical construction site.
whys.evidence: plugins/rin/knowledge/aidlc-shared/code-discipline/cd-021-ports-ship-default-factory.md; plugins/rin/tools/rin-harness-content-digest.ts defaultContentDigestPort.

whys.why: Why is this a wrapping factory rather than a relocated violation?
whys.because: The file holds no logic beyond binding the one capability: consumers depend on ContentDigestPort, no crypto type crosses the boundary, and its co-located test pins the digest of known inputs, which is the shape the sibling path, file and process ports already take.
whys.evidence: plugins/rin/tools/rin-harness-content-digest.test.ts (known sha256 vectors for text, bytes and empty input); the sibling entries for rin-harness-path-operations.ts, rin-harness-sidecar-file-reader.ts and rin-gates/review-process-port.ts in this registry.

whys.why: Why is the binding recorded as an authorised location rather than rewritten?
whys.because: A wrapping factory is where CD-19 says the dependency belongs, so the file was never in debt, and that reclassification is CD-46's discharge; the audit's bare-import detector cannot tell a sanctioned wrapping site from a scattered import without this registry entry.
whys.evidence: rin repo aidlc/spaces/default/memory/project.md § Decided, 2026-08-07: a wrapping factory the CD-19/CD-20 walker flags is an authorised location and that reclassification is CD-46's discharge (knowledge/harness/decisions.md, PR #473).

whyChain.rootCause: The rin plugin needed sha256 hashing in a file whose carve-out decayed on touch, and had no wrapping port for node:crypto to route it through.

reason: Deliberate CD19 wrapping site for the ESLint-compatible CD14 plugin protocol used by ESLint and Oxlint. ESLint and Rule types stay at callback/registration boundaries; configuration consumers receive the owned ClassAuthoringPlugin model. The co-located RuleTester boundary exercises real JS and TypeScript ASTs under operator steer6164120778 item3 (2026-10-14 08:23), not an approval of this draft.

whys.why: Why does this slice depend on the native plugin protocol?
whys.because: CD14 syntax findings must be produced inside the consumer's existing ESLint or Oxlint run.
whys.evidence: PR34 operator steer6163746811: native fragments and dedicated rule.

whys.why: Why must the rule consume external callback and registration types?
whys.because: The engine supplies AST events and diagnostic reporting through its plugin protocol.
whys.evidence: plugins/rin/tools/native-lint/cd14/cd14.eslint-plugin.ts: noClassAuthoring and checkedPlugin.

whys.why: Why confine those types in this file?
whys.because: Consumers can use the owned ClassAuthoringPlugin model without acquiring external ESLint types.
whys.evidence: plugins/rin/tools/native-lint/cd14.eslint.ts imports ClassAuthoringPlugin from the boundary.

whys.why: Why permit a vendor import in the co-located contract test?
whys.because: Real parser-backed RuleTester cases verify ambient AST behavior instead of trusting hand-built nodes.
whys.evidence: https://github.com/HailsTails/aidlc-workflows/pull/34#issuecomment-6164120778 item3.

whys.why: Why is the rule module's create(context) the one protocol boundary, with no inner diagnostic port?
whys.because: create(context) already receives the engine's filename and report callback, so the rule computes the pure classDisposition and calls context.report directly; an inner port would wrap the same boundary twice and was removed.
whys.evidence: https://github.com/HailsTails/aidlc-workflows/pull/34#issuecomment-6164191841 and its clause-by-clause answer: the port is removed; PR34 operator steer6166266007: keep one source.

whyChain.rootCause: Native lint engines own the plugin protocol, so this slice needs an explicit protocol boundary and a real-engine contract-test boundary to avoid distributing vendor coupling through its consumers.

reason: The one adapter that touches the file system for the GitHub bot tooling, behind the TextFileReader, CanonicalPathResolver, PrivateFileReplacer, PrivateFileCreator, FileMover and FileRemover ports. Carried from the minutesarah-shop implementation into the rin plugin so every consumer receives one copy, and extended to write because the user grant and its lock file are persisted in the credential store.

whys.why: Why does local-file-system.ts import node:fs/promises?
whys.because: It implements the file ports: reading file text, resolving a canonical path, replacing a file owner-only through a sibling temporary file and a rename, creating a file owner-only only if it does not exist, moving a file to a new name, and removing a file, each returning a Result instead of throwing
whys.evidence: plugins/rin/tools/github-apps/infrastructure/local-file-system.ts exports readTextFile, resolveCanonicalPath, createPrivateFileReplacer, createPrivateFile, moveFile and removeFile against application/text-file-port.ts and application/private-file-port.ts; nothing else in the package imports node:fs

whys.why: Why must the bot tooling read and write files at all?
whys.because: The identity configuration, the credential store, the app private keys and --body-file bodies live on disk, and the operator's OAuth grant for attachment uploads is persisted per machine in the credential store and refreshed under an exclusive lock file there, because GitHub invalidates the old tokens on every refresh and parallel sessions share the grant
whys.evidence: identity-configuration.ts, file-credential-store.ts and application/read-body-file.ts take readTextFile; file-user-grant-store.ts takes readTextFile and the PrivateFileReplacer that createPrivateFileReplacer builds; exclusive-file-lock.ts takes createPrivateFile, readTextFile, moveFile and removeFile

whys.why: Why do those callers not import node:fs themselves?
whys.because: They depend on the port types, and composition-root.ts injects the one implementation
whys.evidence: file-credential-store.test.ts, identity-configuration.test.ts, read-body-file.test.ts, file-user-grant-store.test.ts and exclusive-file-lock.test.ts run against vi.fn<TextFileReader>(), vi.fn<CanonicalPathResolver>(), vi.fn<PrivateFileReplacer>(), vi.fn<PrivateFileCreator>(), vi.fn<FileMover>() and vi.fn<FileRemover>() fakes

whys.why: Why an authorised location rather than a carve-out?
whys.because: An adapter importing the runtime it wraps is permanent structure, not debt that should decay on touch
whys.evidence: plugins/discipline-core/rules/CD-19/README.md says to use authorised-location for the wrapping file

whys.why: Why one file rather than a second node:fs site for the writes?
whys.because: Replacing the file system binding must touch one file, so the write, create, move and remove capabilities joined the existing reader instead of opening a second wrapping site, and only this adapter sees the node:fs surface
whys.evidence: CD-19 rule text: a dependency swap then touches one file and vendor types never leak inward; local-file-system.ts is the only node:fs import under plugins/rin/tools/github-apps

whyChain.rootCause: The GitHub bot tooling inverts file access behind the text-file and private-file ports, and this adapter is the one place those ports are implemented

whys.why: Why does rs256-signer.ts import node:crypto?

reason: The one adapter that reads the per-user environment for the GitHub bot tooling, behind the UserEnvironment port

whys.why: Why does user-environment.ts import node:os?
whys.because: It implements the UserEnvironment port, naming the home directory with homedir and reading one environment variable
whys.evidence: plugins/rin/tools/github-apps/infrastructure/user-environment.ts exports UserEnvironment and createProcessUserEnvironment

whys.why: Why must the bot tooling know the home directory at all?
whys.because: The app credentials live in one per-user store outside every repository, at ~/.config/rin-github-apps unless RIN_GITHUB_APPS_CREDENTIALS_DIR names another directory
whys.evidence: infrastructure/file-credential-store.ts locateUserStore builds the store directory from UserEnvironment

whys.why: Why is the store outside every repository rather than in the primary checkout as minutesarah had it?
whys.because: The tooling now ships in the rin plugin to many consumers, and one store means each private key exists once and is never inside a checkout that could commit it
whys.evidence: HailsTails/minutesarah-shop#10 handover: recommendation for the harness is one per-user store outside every repository with an environment-variable override

whys.why: Why does file-credential-store.ts not import node:os itself?
whys.because: It takes UserEnvironment as a dependency, so the store location is tested against a plain fake
whys.evidence: file-credential-store.test.ts locateUserStore cases run against an in-memory UserEnvironment

whys.evidence: plugins/discipline-core/rules/CD-19/README.md says to use an authorised location for the wrapping file
